title: Anytime Contracts for AI Services
abstract: arXiv:2610.22781v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI services are prone to moral hazard, as model providers can silently route requests to cheaper, lower-quality models, and the inherent stochasticity of model outputs makes this degradation hard to detect. Contract theory addresses moral hazard by designing payment rules that reward high-quality outputs and prevent strategic overcharging. However, existing frameworks assume interactions of fixed duration, whereas AI services are typically consumed through subscriptions and pay-as-you-go APIs that users can terminate at any time based on observed performance. We show that this flexibility can break standard contracts, opening them up to abuse by either the providers or users. To address this, we extend contract theory to account for unknown exit rules. translated_title: 面向AI服务的随时可退出合约
translated_abstract: AI服务容易受到道德风险的困扰：模型提供方可能悄悄地将请求路由到更便宜、质量更低的模型，而模型输出固有的随机性使得这种质量下降难以被检测。契约理论通过设计奖励高质量输出并防止策略性超额收费的支付规则来应对道德风险。然而，现有框架假设交互具有固定期限，而AI服务通常通过订阅制和按量付费的API来消费，用户可以根据观察到的性能随时终止服务。我们证明了这种灵活性会破坏标准合约，使其容易被提供方或用户滥用。为解决这一问题，我们将契约理论扩展到考虑未知退出规则的情形。我们将该问题形式化为委托-代理博弈，并证明了该设定下预算最优的合约与基于似然比e-过程（原文在此处截断）的任意时刻有效假设检验成正比。
tldr: 该论文将契约理论扩展到用户可随时退出订阅的AI服务场景，证明在此设定下预算最优的合约与基于似然比e-过程的任意时刻有效假设检验成正比，从而防止模型提供方或用户对合约的滥用。
en_tdlr: This paper extends contract theory to AI services with unknown exit rules, showing that budget-optimal contracts in a Principal-Agent game are proportional to anytime-valid hypothesis tests based on likelihood-ratio e-processes, preventing abuse by either providers or users.
